label: copy-phase input token c (fed-back c, recall_idx >= 2)
explanation: Fires when the input during the copy phase is the letter c (the model is reading back its own echoed c), and only from recall_idx >= 2 onward. In the dev split 100% of activation mass is in the copy phase, and in_tok == c accounts for essentially all of it. It never fires on c during the original phase, at the delimiter, or on any other token (a few dozen stray activations). At recall_idx 1 (c being the very first fed-back token after DEL) it is rare and weak (rate 0.005). Magnitude: low-quartile examples are c inputs early in the copy phase (recall_idx 1-2), and the top examples are c inputs late in the copy phase, often the first c of a doubled cc. That suggests magnitude rises with copy position, but I only checked this on examples. The firing rate is flat at ~0.033 for recall_idx >= 2 and does not depend on out_tok, prev_tok or L.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. The test split gives precision 1.000, recall 0.967, F1 0.983 and mass recall 0.998. There are 0 false positives.

Nearly all of the 2510 test misses are weak activations (0.01 to 0.06 of max) on c inputs at recall_idx 1. They carry only 0.2% of the activation mass. Adding recall_idx==1 to the predicate does not help: c & recall_idx==1 has precision 0.146, so excluding that position is correct.
Phase claims hold. Activation share is 0.000 in the original phase and at the delimiter, and all of it is in the copy phase. Non-c inputs have at most 9 active steps per token across 6.4M steps.

The magnitude claim holds on the full split, not just on the example sequences. c & recall_idx==2 covers 78% of the bottom activation quartile and 0% of the top. c & recall_idx>=5 covers 1.5% of the bottom quartile and 62% of the top. So magnitude rises with copy position.

Wording problem: the stated firing rate of 0.033 is per step over all copy steps at that recall_idx, not the rate on c inputs. Conditional on a copy-phase c input at recall_idx>=2, the feature fires nearly every time (precision 1, recall about 0.97). Rate does not depend on out_tok (about 0.024 to 0.026 for every out_tok). The top examples look like the first c of a doubled cc, but c & out_tok==c covers only 9% of the top quartile, so that is incidental, and it does not contradict the explanation.
